title: audit-telemetry-edge-proxy-offline-queueing-and-splunk-datadog-adapters
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build an edge-proxy + adapter pattern for audit telemetry that provides robust delivery guarantees to downstream SIEMs (Splunk HEC, generic webhook sinks like Datadog) while supporting temporary network outages, tenant rate tiers, and ordered delivery where required. This ticket implements the proxy queueing, signed envelope format, observable ack model, and adapter-layer backoff/retry semantics. We aim for at-least-once delivery by default with optional exactly-once tooling for customers who opt into sequence tokens and idempotency keys. The proxy should maintain tenant isolation, per-tenant size limits, and per-route SLOs (p99 latency target for accepted acks).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Edge proxy persists events to a write-ahead queue before acknowledging ingestion and exposes per-tenant queue depth metrics.
2) Splunk HEC adapter supports HEC token rotation, batching, and 207/5xx handling with exponential backoff and DLQ for persistent failures.
3) Generic webhook adapter (Datadog/other) supports synchronous 2xx/3xx ack semantics, dedup-id support, and jittered retry policy with configurable max attempts.
4) End-to-end test with simulated 30s outage shows no telemetry loss and delivery within configured DLQ thresholds.
5) Console dashboard surfaces per-route success rate, retry counts, median time-to-delivery, and DLQ size.
6) Design doc and security review completed and approved before rollout.
7) Post-deploy chaos test executed with runbook and rollback criteria documented.
notes: 2025-02-14: Spike completed investigating HEC idempotency options; Splunk recommends idempotent tokens via metadata + explicit ACK semantics for batch endpoints.
2025-02-20: Chosen design: proxy writes signed envelope (base64 + hmac with customer key) to WAL and returns 202 to producer as soon as queued. Adapter polls WAL with tenant sharding.
2025-02-24: Implemented local queue persistence using rocksdb-backed segments with configurable compaction and per-tenant byte quota.
2025-02-28: Initial Splunk HEC adapter supports batching by size and time; added support for 207 multi-status handling and partial retries for failed items.
2025-03-03: Added Datadog adapter prototype using webhook retry headers and idempotency-key header passthrough; metrics plumbing to Grafana in progress.
comments: PM (Sofia Martinez): Please ensure the console exposes per-customer SLA tier mapping so support can triage impact during outages.
Security (Marco Li): Envelope signing must use KMS-backed keys and include tenant id + monotonic sequence to help detect replay attacks. Recommend HMAC-SHA256 with key rotation metadata.
Design review (Katherine Wu): Agree with WAL-first approach. Concern: per-tenant WAL growth under bursty audit storms. Action: add eviction policy and soft-limits with customer notifications.
Eng review (Ravi Patel): Suggest exposing an at-most-once mode for low-sensitivity flows where duplicate suppression costs outweigh risk; add explicit opt-in flag.
implementation_notes:
- WAL-first ingestion to minimize producer-visible latency and avoid data loss on proxy restarts.
- Signed envelope fields: tenant_id | envelope_id | seq_no (optional) | timestamp | payload_sha256 | hmac_version | key_id.
- Adapter responsibilities: unpack envelope, validate HMAC (via KMS key access), expand batch, call downstream with per-item idempotency header if present.
- Backoff: jittered exponential backoff with initial 500ms, max 60s, max attempts configurable per customer tier.
- DLQ: per-tenant compacted topic with retention policy 7 days by default, flag to escalate to support for enterprise tiers.
- Ordering: provide sequence token passthrough for customers that require strictly ordered ingest; this disables parallelism for that tenant-route and will be documented as higher-latency mode.
- Observability: expose metrics: enqueue_latency_ms, dequeue_latency_ms, delivery_success_rate, retries_per_event, dlq_inserts, in_progress_per_tenant.
- Cost control: samples and metadata-only mode for heavy customers to bound egress costs.
